newsitem.title: UK: Former Co-op chief dismisses break up attempt.
newsitem.headline: Former Co-op chief dismisses break up attempt.

text.p: Sir Dennis Landau, former chief executive of Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society said on Tuesday an attempt to break it up was ill-conceived.
"The whole thing is an absolute bloody nonsense," Landau said of a recent approach by Andrew Regan's Lanica Trust to the CWS about buying some of its non-food businesses.
Entrepreneur Regan is believed to be targeting the Co-operative Bank, which is owned by the CWS, or the society's Co-operative Insurance Society (CIS).
CWS has interests ranging from supermarkets and farms to funeral parlours and travel agencies but has been criticised for dwindling returns, prompting suggestions of a break-up.
Last week the Co-op Bank reported record pretax profits of 45.5 million pounds and reiterated that it is not up for sale.
Regan is reported to have approached the Bank of England to ask it to rule that he would be a fit and proper person to run the bank.

But Landau said the reported 500 million pound approach by a company partly-owned by Lanica to the CWS for parts of its non-foods business appeared not to have been properly researched as it did not take account of the complex way the CWS is structured.
Landau, who retired as chief executive of CWS five years ago, was speaking at a briefing on the annual results of British trade union bank Unity Trust Bank, of which he is chairman.

He described the approach as "almost immature" but acknowledged it had been healthy for the movement because, as with any takeover attempt, it had made the management look at themselves. "I think it is healthy...self-criticism is not a bad thing," he said.
Shares in Lanica, which were star performers last year on speculation over Regan's intentions, were suspended on February 10 at 19.50 each.
Landau said he was "disgusted" that Lanica's shares had not yet been relisted.
